title: CI/CD, and what changes when the system uses AI
description: Continuous integration and delivery in plain words: what each means, the pipeline stage by stage, Jenkins and its alternatives, and the evaluation stage an AI system needs before it is deployed.

title: TDD, BDD and SDD: write what “correct” means first
description: Test-Driven, Behaviour-Driven and Spec-Driven Development explained one by one: what each writes first, how TDD and BDD compare, and why SDD has grown with AI coding agents.

title: Architecture patterns, and where microservices fit
description: The main software architecture patterns in one picture, then a close look at microservices: what they cost, what Docker, Kubernetes and OpenShift each add, and the patterns that keep them working.

title: Hallucinations, tracing and evaluation: trusting an AI system in production
description: Why AI systems give confident wrong answers, what that looks like in a real system, and how design, tracing with Langfuse and evaluation make them rare and visible.

title: Workflow or agent? How much autonomy to give an AI system
description: A workflow follows the steps you wrote; an agent chooses its own. What each is good at, the levels in between, and how to decide where the model belongs.

title: Four agentic patterns you should know
description: Reflection, tool use, planning and multi-agent: what each pattern is, when it earns its cost, and where each one goes wrong. With a diagram for every one.

title: Sanderson’s laws of magic, applied to AI agents
description: A fantasy author’s three rules for designing magic systems, read as a design review for AI agents: understood before it is trusted, limits over powers, and depth before more tools.

title: MCP in plain words: how AI agents reach your systems
description: What the Model Context Protocol is, the problem it removes, what a server looks like in Python, and how to design tools a model can use safely.

title: How I work with AI: a system, not autopilot
description: Understand it first, write the rules down, delegate small, review every line, verify the result. How I use Claude Code, Orca and MCP without handing over the decisions.

title: The pick and roll of AI agents
description: Two players, two roles, one read. How the most common play in basketball explains an orchestrator and a specialist agent working together, and the turnovers that break both.

title: What is a Forward Deployed Engineer?
description: The role in plain words: an engineer who builds inside the customer's problem. What they do, how it differs from the roles next to it, and why AI made it grow.

title: What really matters in AI engineering today
description: A new AI announcement every day, and much of it fades within weeks. The parts that last: the harness, skills, MCP, RAG, LangGraph and Langfuse, and the trends I approach with caution.

title: How to build a RAG system that survives production
description: Retrieval-augmented generation in plain words and pictures: the two pipelines, chunking, search by meaning, and what separates a demo from a system your company can rely on.

title: n8n automation: how to build a workflow step by step
description: What n8n is, how a workflow runs from trigger to action, and a worked example with Docker Compose, MySQL and a REST API. Ends with what to check before a workflow goes to production.
